chunks: And in the narration of ʿUmar ibn Yazīd:
"Except one who breaks his fast upon an intoxicant, or one bearing enmity, or one involved with shāhayn, and it is chess."

key_terms.شَاهَيْنِ: a term explained here as referring to chess
key_terms.صَاحِبَ: one associated with or engaged in
key_terms.مُشَاحِنٍ: a person harboring enmity or rancor

ai.seo_question: Who is excluded from the virtue of fasting in this narration from Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This narration excludes certain people from the virtue under discussion, specifically those who break their fast with an intoxicant, those who harbor rancor, and those associated with chess. It links the spiritual reward of fasting with both outward conduct and inward moral state.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1839 - In the narration of Umar ibn Yazid:
"Except for those who break their fast with an intoxicant, harbor enmity [Mushahinan], or are engaged with shahīn (which refers to chess)."
